# Syrtis v1.4.0

**Settings gains an Accounts page, and Syrtis can read Cursor's encrypted sign-in once you allow it.** Antigravity's Gemini quota bars are back, and agy 1.4.x logins can be captured again. Read "Before you update" first: the usage engine moved, and going back needs a backup.

## Before you update

- **The first launch re-reads your Claude logs once.** ([#269](https://github.com/Nanako0129/Syrtis-Windows/pull/269)) On the maintainer's Windows test PC the first launch rewrote all 246 Claude cache files within about 10.6 seconds, and the next launch rewrote none. Totals were not compared before and after. Droid, Qwen, Roo Code, Kilo Code and Cline are also read again once; how long that takes was not measured.
- **Going back to v1.3.0 or earlier loses Claude history that only the cache still holds, unless you back it up before you install.** An older version rebuilds the new Claude cache from your logs and drops those turns. The update dialog's Install starts the new version at once, so the copy has to come first: quit Syrtis and any other tokscale program, then copy the folder `%APPDATA%\tokscale\cache\source-message-cache-v2\claude` (or the same path under `TOKSCALE_CONFIG_DIR`, if you set it) to a new folder outside `tokscale\cache`. The checked copy and restore commands, and the order the restore has to follow, are in [vendor/ENGINE.md](https://github.com/Nanako0129/Syrtis-Windows/blob/main/vendor/ENGINE.md) under "Windows backup and rollback of the Claude cache". They were run against a scratch folder, not a real Claude cache.
- **Antigravity's account list moved off your roaming profile.** ([#274](https://github.com/Nanako0129/Syrtis-Windows/pull/274)) The account list, the removed-account list, the current binding and the automatic-capture switch now live in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\TokenBar\antigravity.json`, moved once per PC at launch. The old roaming copy stays for one release. If you go back to an older version, it reads that old removed-account list, so an account you removed can be captured again.
- **A tray selection pinned to an Antigravity primary model window shows no value after the update.** ([#271](https://github.com/Nanako0129/Syrtis-Windows/pull/271)) The primary account now reads the quota summary. Pick it again.

## Accounts and Cursor

- **Settings has an Accounts page.** ([#267](https://github.com/Nanako0129/Syrtis-Windows/pull/267), [#264](https://github.com/Nanako0129/Syrtis-Windows/pull/264)) Claude extra folders, Antigravity accounts with automatic capture, and Cursor usage sync (moved from General) sit there, each with a one-line summary and an info button. Turning on Cursor sync opens a confirmation with Cancel and Continue, and nothing is turned on until you press Continue. Syrtis asks only while the notice is unanswered. After Sync Now, keyboard focus stays in the Cursor section. The maintainer checked the page on the test PC.
- **Cursor's encrypted sign-in can be read after you allow it.** ([#273](https://github.com/Nanako0129/Syrtis-Windows/pull/273)) Cursor 3.27 and later can store its sign-in encrypted, and Syrtis could not read it. Settings → Accounts → Cursor now says "Cursor stores its sign-in encrypted. Syrtis needs your permission to read it." with the button "Allow reading Cursor's encrypted sign-in…". The confirmation ("Allow access") explains that Syrtis unlocks the key in Cursor's "Local State" file, that Windows does not ask, so this is the only check, and that the sign-in goes only to cursor.com. "Withdraw" takes the permission back. On the test PC, with Cursor 3.28.7 set to store its sign-in encrypted, Allow synced it, a relaunch synced without asking again, and Withdraw brought the permission line back. Other Cursor versions were not tried.
- **A failed Cursor sync shows its reason code**, as "Cursor usage couldn't be synced (<code>). Syrtis will try again later." ([#273](https://github.com/Nanako0129/Syrtis-Windows/pull/273)) Tests cover it; no failing sync was seen on a device.
- **Grok Bot's Cursor fallback no longer sends a Cursor sign-in that is not a session token**, including the encrypted form. ([#273](https://github.com/Nanako0129/Syrtis-Windows/pull/273)) Tests cover it.

## Antigravity

- **The Gemini Weekly and Five Hour bars are back.** ([#271](https://github.com/Nanako0129/Syrtis-Windows/pull/271)) Two of the three Antigravity scopes on the test PC had stopped receiving Gemini quota in mid-October. After the change the card showed both bars and Gemini 4 Argon Weekly; Gemini Five Hour read 92.85% left against the agy CLI's 93%. A bucket label that repeats its group name is shortened ("Gemini 4 Argon · Weekly"); a test covers that, and it was not seen on screen. The `arm64` request header was not run on an arm64 machine.
- **agy 1.4.x logins that store no account identity can be captured.** ([#272](https://github.com/Nanako0129/Syrtis-Windows/pull/272)) agy 1.4.8 stopped storing an `id_token`, and Capture stopped with "agy's saved login doesn't say which Google account it is". Syrtis now identifies the account from Google's answer. On the test PC, Capture before the change showed that error and wrote nothing; after, it showed no error and rewrote the captured login. The account there was already captured, so a new account appearing was not seen, and removal after an agy sign-out and sign-in was not run on the device.
- **The weekly allowance shows on the local IDE card.** ([#259](https://github.com/Nanako0129/Syrtis-Windows/pull/259)) While the Antigravity IDE runs, its card now shows the weekly rows next to the per-model windows. Seen on the test PC.
- **Antigravity Extension usage is recognized** under the Antigravity tab. ([#261](https://github.com/Nanako0129/Syrtis-Windows/pull/261)) No Windows extension database was available to try it on.
- **A merged Antigravity card says why its pace is missing.** ([#275](https://github.com/Nanako0129/Syrtis-Windows/pull/275)) When the captured account behind the merged card fails its own quota check, the pace line reads "Pace unavailable · this account's quota check failed". Tests cover it; it was not seen on a device.
- **Multi-account fixes.** ([#274](https://github.com/Nanako0129/Syrtis-Windows/pull/274)) A removed account stays removed through a token refresh. While settings cannot be saved, Capture, automatic capture and Remove are off, and Settings says "Syrtis can't save its Antigravity settings on this PC right now, so Capture, automatic capture and Remove are off until Syrtis restarts." If Remove cannot update the account list, nothing is removed and Settings says "Syrtis couldn't update its account list, so nothing was removed. Try again." The Claude and Antigravity sections update in place, so reopening Settings neither fails nor loses controls, and keyboard focus stays on the automatic-capture switch. The reopen and the switch focus were checked on the test PC; the rest is covered by tests. Reading a Claude config folder's login no longer blocks Claude Code from saving it (not seen with Claude Code), and an account with an error is not picked for the window card (the fallback with account pills was not run on a device).

## Also in this release

- **Claude Desktop's MSIX package data is found.** ([#257](https://github.com/Nanako0129/Syrtis-Windows/pull/257)) Syrtis looks under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages\Claude_*\LocalCache\Roaming\Claude` as well as `%APPDATA%\Claude`, and prefers an unexpired login over a stale copy. Tests cover it; the test PC was not used.
- **A custom OpenCode database is scanned.** ([#263](https://github.com/Nanako0129/Syrtis-Windows/pull/263), [#266](https://github.com/Nanako0129/Syrtis-Windows/pull/266)) `OPENCODE_DB` and `scanner.opencodeDbPaths` in tokscale's `settings.json` are read, and a relative `OPENCODE_DB` is resolved the way OpenCode does. A changed `OPENCODE_DB` needs a restart. Tested with child processes against a fixture database; no real OpenCode database was used.
- **The Models view keeps its rows during a refresh.** ([#262](https://github.com/Nanako0129/Syrtis-Windows/pull/262)) Cost, shares and the "Prices updated" hint read "Checking" until the new report arrives. Tests cover it; it was not seen on a device.
- **The README explains how to include Claude Code usage from WSL**, with `TOKSCALE_EXTRA_DIRS`. ([#156](https://github.com/Nanako0129/Syrtis-Windows/pull/156))
- **Usage engine changes** ([#261](https://github.com/Nanako0129/Syrtis-Windows/pull/261), [#269](https://github.com/Nanako0129/Syrtis-Windows/pull/269)); none was compared against Windows data, so no totals are quoted:
  - Claude input is taken from the line that carries the cache split instead of a larger prompt snapshot, so Claude input can fall for some requests. How much depends on your logs.
  - Roo Code, Kilo Code and Cline tasks under `%APPDATA%\Code\User\globalStorage\<extension-id>\tasks` are read. A positive cost the extension reports is kept; Roo and Kilo rows dated 2025-11-02 UTC or later no longer count cache buckets twice in input.
  - Hermes reasoning tokens are counted once, Qwen's cached prompt tokens leave its input, and Droid replies are counted on the date each was written.
  - Rows are priced from the hinted vendor's own entry instead of a reseller's, and Antigravity's `gemini-3.8-flash-control`, `-high`, `-low`, `-tiered` and `-n` labels fold into `gemini-3.8-flash`. Costs can change; the size was not measured on Windows.
  - OpenRouter's published cache rates are kept, and Codex rollouts compressed as `.jsonl.zst` are read.
  - A Goose database at `%APPDATA%\Block\goose\data\sessions\sessions.db` is detected. The test PC has no Goose data, so this was not seen.

## Known limits

- If a settings save fails at the wrong moment, a just-captured Antigravity account can lack a list row after Syrtis exits, or a removal can last only until it exits.
- A Claude config folder path of 260 characters or more cannot be read for its login.
- Clicking an errored account's pill stores the choice, but the card stays on the live account until the errored one recovers.
- The missing-folder icon on a Claude row has no glyph.
- Whether a cloud placeholder that is not yet downloaded can be read as a Claude login was not measured.
